      <title>Israel med ny offensiv – tre drept</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/israel-med-ny-offensiv-_-tre-drept-1.18084431</link>
      <description>Israels hær sier den har innledet en operasjon i Hamas-kontrollerte områder i Gaza
Israel har innledet en militæroperasjon i det sentrale Gaza vest for den såkalte gule linjen, som har skilt Hamas-kontrollerte og israelsk-kontrollerte områder siden våpenhvilen trådte i kraft i fjor. Det opplyser militæret til AFP.
Vitner sier at israelske stridsvogner rullet inn på hovedveien Salahudeen, vest for den såkalte gule linjen som markerer grensen for de to tredjedelene av Gazastripen som fortsatt er under israelsk kontroll.
Den såkalte gule linjen ble etablert etter våpenhvilen i oktober 2025 og skiller israelskkontrollerte og palestinske soner i Gazastripen. Israelske styrker har gradvis flyttet den gule linjen og utvidet området under direkte militær kontroll i Gaza.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Braathen med ny maktdemonstrasjon: – Jeg er så full av følelser</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/braathen-med-ny-maktdemonstrasjon_-_-jeg-er-sa-full-av-folelser-1.18082207</link>
      <description>Norsk-brasilianske Lucas Pinheiro Braathen (26) fortsetter å ydmyke konkurrentene.
Etter seier i storslalåm-starten i Sölden, fortsatte han med seier i slalåm i finske Levi søndag.
– Det er så godt å være her i Levi. Jeg er så full av følelser nå. Jeg skal prøve å ta selvtilliten med meg videre til neste renn, sier Braathen selv i arenaintervjuet.
Clément Noël ble nummer to, 56 hundredeler bak vinneren. Atle Lie McGrath ble beste norske på 7. plass.
– Det er hans bakke. Han elsker den. Han elsker disse forholdene, sier TV 2-ekspert Kjetil Jansrud på direkten.
– Han er fremdeles norsk, men han representerer Brasil. Vi skulle gjerne ha sett det norske flagget bak navnet hans, fortsetter Jansrud.
Dette er den tredje vinteren der Braathen representerer Brasil etter at han brøt med Norges Skiforbund.
– For en kjøring. Det er store, store avstander i en bakke som Levi, sa TV 2-ekspert Jansrud etter Braathens første omgang.
Han ledet med hele 65 hundredeler til toeren, Clément Noël, før finaleomgangen.

– Det Lucas gjør det er helt i egen klasse, sa Timon Haugan til TV 2 etter første omgang.
– Jeg fikk meg en på tygga, sier McGrath om finaleomgangen.
Oscar Andreas Sandvik kjørte seg opp fra 29. plass til nummer 11.
Både Timon Haugan og Henrik Kristoffersen tapte halvannet sekund til Braathen i første omgang. Begge fortsatte å skuffe i andre omgang og ble henholdsvis 18 og 19.
– Jeg kjørte i en stein, forteller Kristoffersen til TV 2.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Vind og kaos-skyting: Kirkeeide vant fellesstarten etter åtte (!) bom</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/vind-og-kaos-skyting_-kirkeeide-vant-fellesstarten-etter-atte-___-bom-1.18082184</link>
      <description>Maren Kirkeeide stakk av med seieren på kvinnenes fellesstart i skiskyting på Geilo søndag.
Lørdagens sprintsensasjon Guro Ytterhus imponerte igjen og tok andreplass 14,4 sekunder bak Kirkeeide.
Juni Arnekleiv ledet etter to fulle hus, men på tredje skyting ble det kaos. Sterk vind gjorde at flere av utøverne bommet mange ganger, og Arnekleiv røk på fire bom.
Dermed tok Karoline Knotten over teten. Men på siste skyting, så haglet skuddene utenfor blinkene nok en gang.
Og plutselig var Kirkeeide i tet etter hele åtte (!) bom. Få løpere måtte ut i flere strafferunder, men likevel holdt hun ledelsen helt til mål.
– Det var en merkelig fellesstart. Det var veldig mange som bommet. Det var tydeligvis ikke så lett som man skulle tro, sier Kirkeeide til NRK etter seieren.
Karoline Knotten tok tredjeplass.
Ingrid Landmark Tandrevold, Marthe Kråkstad Johansen, Karoline Knotten og nevnte Kirkeeide er forhåndsuttatt til verdenscupstarten i finske Kontiolahti senere i måneden. Kvinnenes tropp skal til slutt bestå av seks løpere.</description>

      <title>Flystansen i USA: Bytting av kabel mulig årsak</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/flystansen-i-usa_-bytting-av-kabel-mulig-arsak-1.18082036</link>
      <description>USAs transportminister Sean Duffy sier utskiftning av en kobbertråd kan være årsaken til den omfattende flystansen fredag.
Flere enn 15.000 flygninger ble forsinket eller innstilt da amerikanske luftfartsmyndigheter FAA i fire timer nektet alle fly å ta av på grunn av forstyrrelser i flykontrollen.
På en pressekonferanse lørdag sa transportminister Duffy at problemene kan ha oppstått som følge av arbeidet med å bytte ut gamle kobberkabler med fiber ved et av FAAs anlegg.
Ministeren oppgav også navnet på selskapet han mente hadde forsårsaket problemene. Hendelsen skal granskes videre.
Det er fremdeles etterslep etter fredagens problemer. Lørdag er flere enn 10.000 flygninger innstilt eller forsinket, ifølge FlightAware.</description>

      <description>Det brenner kraftig i en enebolig på en gård i Trondheimsveien i Lillestrøm.
– Det er full fyr i hele bygningen, opplyser oppdragsleder i politiet, Ronny Mangseth.
– Brannvesenet er fremme og er i gang med slukking. Det er kontroll på alle fire beboere på stedet, sier han.
Ved 17:20-tiden opplyser politiet at det fortsatt brenner i boligen, og at arbeidet med slukking vil ta tid.
En person skal ha fått i seg noe røyk.
Det skal ikke være fare for spredning til låve eller andre bygninger på gården.
Ifølge politiet er det ikke kjent hva som er årsaken til brannen, og de vil etterforske saken videre.</description>

      <title>Solbakken overrasker – Aasgaard inn i startelleveren</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/solbakken-overrasker-_-aasgaard-inn-i-startelleveren-1.18081988</link>
      <description>Ståle Solbakken har valgt ut følgende ellever til kampen mot Wales på Ullevaal:
Egil Selvik – Julian Ryerson, Kristoffer Ajer, Torbjørn Heggem, David Møller Wolfe – Sander Berge, Martin Ødegaard, Thelo Aasgaard – Antonio Nusa, Erling Braut Haaland, Oscar Bobb.
– Jeg må innrømme at jeg er noe overrasket. Men da tenker vel Solbakken at han passer bedre til denne kampen enn det Patrick Berg gjør akkurat nå, sier NRK-ekspert Andrine Hegerberg om at Aasgaards inntog i startelleveren.
Han er én av fire bytter som er gjort fra elleveren som møtte Portugal i forrige nasjonsligakamp.
Leo Østigård, Andreas Schjelderup og Patrick Berg er henvist til benken, mens Fredrik Aursnes ikke er med på grunn av en skade.
Samtidig er det nok en gang Egil Selvik som skal vokte buret for Norge.
– Jeg er først og fremst stolt, men også spent. Det blir en viktig kamp for oss, så det gjelder å gi jernet. Vi har noe å revansjere, sier Selvik til TV 2.
På motsatt banehalvdel starter Wales med følgende mannskap:
Karl Darlow – Neco Williams, Joe Rodon, Ben Davies, Jay Dasilva – Harry Wilson, Ethan Ampadu, Liam Cullen, Daniel James – Lewis Koumas, Brennan Johnson.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Kjørte ned tre personer</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sorlandet/kjorte-ned-tre-personer--1.18081598</link>
      <description>En eldre kvinnelig bilfører kjørte ned tre personer i Lyngdal.
To personer på sparkesykkel ble truffet av bilen, før den fortsatte og traff en tredje person.
Denne personen ble hentet med ambulanse, mens de to på sparkesykkel fikk mindre skader. Det melder politiet på Agder.
Bilisten er en kvinne i 80-årene, og hun skal ha kjørt bilen opp på fortauet.
Bilen skal også ha vært borti et bygg som har fått skader.</description>

Passengers on a Victoria to Toronto flight struggled to get off the ground due to an incident with a tow vehicle and an Air Canada aircraft.

The incident occurred at 12:20 p.m. on Wednesday, Nov. 18 at the Victoria International Airport (YYJ), just five minutes before the flight’s scheduled take-off, leading to a lengthy delay for passengers on flight AC1902 to Toronto Pearson International Airport (YYZ).

Erin Brocklebank, Victoria Airport Authority spokesperson, tells CHEK in an email, “An operational incident involving an Air Canada Rouge aircraft and a tow vehicle occurred today at Victoria International Airport (YYJ) while the aircraft was being pushed back.”

Brocklebank says the flight was cancelled, and that “alternate travel arrangements have been made for affected passengers.”

YYJ’s flight status for Wednesday showed the Air Canada Rouge flight was scheduled for 12:25 p.m., and had been delayed to 6:10 p.m.

No injuries have been reported at this time. Travellers are advised to contact Air Canada for additional information.

Around 1:40 p.m., Turbine Traveller posted about the incident on X saying the incident occurred “during pushback at Victoria International Airport. The pushback towbar sheared.”

The metal pushback towbar attaches to the aircraft’s nose and the ground vehicle, which then pushes the plane backward, away from a gate or parking stand.

Air Canada Rouge flight AC1902, operated by an Airbus A320-200 (C-GFDU), has been involved in a ground incident during pushback at Victoria International Airport. The pushback towbar sheared. The aircraft was scheduled to operate a flight to Toronto. https://t.co/wqaCdWXVAr

B.C. politicians are expressing concern over the potential sale of Vancouver-based telecommunications giant Telus.

Quebecor has put in an unsolicited bid for the company, which is responsible for thousands of jobs in the province.

Opposition NDP leader Jennifer Whiteside on Wednesday urged premier-designate Lorne Doerkson to object to the federal government about the sale.

“British Columbians already pay among the highest cell phone bills in the developed world, and reducing competition would drive bills up even higher,” Whiteside said in a news release.

“Lorne Doerkson should take immediate action by writing to the federal government to urge them to reject this deal.”

Whiteside wrote Doerkson a letter, urging him to be a “fierce advocate” for the province on the issue.

Doerkson, who is not sworn into office until Friday, said in a statement that “my focus is on ensuring British Columbians have choice, competitive prices and reliable service in mobile services.

“As well, I want to ensure local jobs are preserved,” he said.

“There are legitimate questions raised by a change in ownership and must be fully considered as part of any approval process.”

Telus’ board hasn’t decided whether to accept the offer. Any sale would require approval from the federal government, which has competition and telecommunications rules. It would also mean Canada’s big four telecom providers would fall to three.

Prime Minister Mark Carney, in China Wednesday, said he wants to see investment in telecommunications, but also a competitive market that produces competitive prices for Canadians.

“Depending on the market structure, the form of oligopoly can lead to more competition with fewer players under certain circumstances,” said Carney.

“So it depends on the market structure aspect of it, and we need to take an informed decision on that, and when push comes to shove on any decision – when we can have more competition, better services for Canadians, that’s where we’re going to land.”

The Downtown Victoria Business Association is launching a new holiday campaign this year, the first time in roughly eight years that the Lights of Wonder display will not be returning.

From Nov. 21 to Dec. 27, the DVBA’s “Unwrap Downtown” holiday campaign will offer free horse-drawn trolley rides, interactive pop-ups, live entertainment and more in Victoria.

The campaign also includes “warm cups of cheer,” where participating businesses offer free warm beverages and treats, free holiday photos at the Bay Centre, and special promotions at participating businesses every Sunday.

During the campaign, two information huts will also be set up on Government Street near Pandora Avenue and Courtenay Street from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays and Sundays, with workers providing maps, information about activities, and free “warm cups of cheer” tickets.

The goal of the campaign is to give downtown businesses a boost during the holiday season. A full list of activities and schedules can be found on the DVBA website.

A map of the free, hop-on, hop-off horse-drawn trolley route is shown below. The trolleys are scheduled to arrive every 20 minutes, approximately.

“Unwrap Downtown is about creating experiences that you can’t get shopping online or in a big-box store,” said Jeff Bray, CEO of the DVBA. 

“It’s about discovering a new favourite business, enjoying something unexpected and magical with your family, and enjoying everything that makes downtown Victoria such a special place,” he said.

The campaign is also receiving support from the City of Victoria. 

“The vibrancy of our city comes from the one-of-a-kind businesses that make Victoria such a special place,” said Victoria Mayor Marianne Alto.

Lights of Wonder unplugged

Earlier this year, the Downtown Victoria Business Association announced that the free Lights of Wonder display would not be returning this year.

The display launched in 2019 and typically ran through the entire month of December. However, in May, the DVBA said that the display would not be returning for 2026 due to the displays needing costly repairs, and because the DVBA had trouble finding a sponsor.

The display had grown to include a Ferris wheel, live music and performances, food and alcohol vendors, and more – but it took hundreds of thousands of dollars to set up and weeks to install.

]]> 1362351 DND finds exploded munition scraps at project site near Goose Spit, B.C. https://cheknews.ca/dnd-finds-exploded-munition-scraps-at-project-site-near-goose-spit-b-c-1362298/ Wed, 18 Nov 2026 21:16:11 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1362298

Beach walkers at Goose Spit are being reminded of potential delays or detours while the Department of National Defence scours the historical defence lands for hazardous material, including unexploded ordnance.

The post DND finds exploded munition scraps at project site near Goose Spit, B.C. appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Beach walkers at the popular Goose Spit coastal park are being reminded of potential delays or detours while the Department of National Defence is scanning and excavating the historical defence lands for hazardous material, including unexploded ordnance (UXO) that date back to the Second World War.

The DND’s surface and sub-surface scanning project of the defence lands near Goose Spit, south of Comox, started on Nov. 1 and is expected to continue through Dec. 15.

Maj. Ward Trythall, regional civil planner for the military and the project manager of the UXO Goose Spit scanning project, says a third-party consultant called Munitions Response Services (MRS) is handling the fieldwork with a crew of six to a dozen members.

“They’re, the experts in unexploded ordnance scanning and have done significant works across the country. And within B.C., certainly they’re still working on the UXO removal project in Vernon at what’s known as the Vernon Commons, and have been doing so for many years,” said Trythall.

On Nov. 13, Trythall, said the team had completed phase one of scanning and were starting phase two, where crews begin to excavate and retrieve their findings.

Findings reported so far

After completing the first phase of scanning, crews found pieces of unexploded ordnance, but none intact to date. 

“To date, we have not found any UXO, defined as actually intact, unexploded ordnance,” he said, adding, “We have found some, what we call munition scrap, which is pieces of ordnance that are on the land. For the most part, that’s been old, small arms ammunition, expended small arms ammunition. Typically they’ve been what we call blank rounds, so they were used for training, and a couple of pieces of exploded munition of some sort.”

According to Trythall, the area on Goose Spit was an active Canadian military training site in World War II. However, there are gaps in the land records in terms of risk assessments, so this project is the DND’s commitment to due diligence and risk assessment activities required on the defence lands.

He says they’ve uncovered mainly fragments, adding that the bulk of their findings are old steel rods and pieces of fence posts.

Safety near potential explosives

Now in phase two, crews are starting to dig out their findings. 

Trythall explains it’s “where we are actually going along and excavating each of the targets, we’re only approximately five, 10 per cent in so far and that’s the extent of what we found.”

Crews are excavating these decades-old items by hand.

“So far, our expectation is that most of the munition scrap dates from the Second World War. We started the project, having done a thorough record search of modern Canadian Armed Forces records, and we’re able to satisfy ourselves that in modern times, records dating back in theory, similar to the early 1970s, that there was no expectation that there would be dangerous, unexploded ordnance on the spit, because the area had not been approved for use of those types of ammunition on the spit in that period up to today.”

However, they treat each retrieval as a potential risk and that’s why the public is being asked to keep a 60 metre distance from the exclusion zone.

“Every target represents a risk until we’ve identified it satisfactorily. So what we’re establishing around the target, any given excavation is that 60 metre exclusion zone. So within that zone, the operators are the only ones inside that for safety purposes, the archeological team moves back,” he says.

The exclusion zone is marked with signage and crews are on site to provide direction near the area.

He asks the public to be mindful when crews are working at the edge of the defence lands property where it overlaps with the public beach.

“And because the DND lands extend right to what’s known as the natural boundary, or the high tide mark, if we are excavating a target that’s right at the edge of the land boundary with the intertidal zone…That 60-metre exclusion zone can impact travel along the beach and that is really our biggest safety concern for us,” he says.

“When members of the public encounter those signs, our simple ask is, please respect them and understand that those exclusion zones are for their safety, just in case we do happen upon something that is dangerous, so that an accident, if it ever occurred while they’re excavating, has a very limited impact upon anybody who may be outside that 60-metre zone.”

First Nation land

Tryhall adds that project was initiated due to the Goose Spit lands being divested by B.C. to the Ko’mox First Nation’s treaty settlement lands.

“Because DND was occupying those lands under an Order in Council, granted by the provincial government 70 years ago, the arrangement and agreement within the treaty is that certain lands will be divested to the K’ómoks Nation and the K’ómoks Nation will grant a subsequent tenure to National Defence for our continued use, where we have uses on the Goose Spit Peninsula right now.”

K’ómoks First Nation (KFN) explains how the Goose Spit is broken up into four different parcels: “The first is the stretch of road, which is governed by Area B of the CVRD. The second is the HMCS Quadra Cadet Base. The third piece is our Indian Reserve #3, and the fourth is what we have been calling the ‘tip’ of the spit, which was offered and accepted by KFN as part of the Agreement in Principle.”

“There is currently no lease with DND for the use of our reserve lands,” says the KFN.

The nation is currently negotiating a lease agreement with the DND to use the “tip” of the Spit for specific purposes when needed.

“The HMCS Quadra Cadet Base is legally owned by B.C. and is being used by DND under an Order in Council with Canada. The Treaty, if approved, will include the transfer of the full Goose Spit to the KFN, including HMCS Quadra, which includes the cadet camp,” adds the KFN.

]]> 1362320 Minister says discussions with Meta ‘confidential’ following reports of possible deal https://cheknews.ca/minister-says-discussions-with-meta-confidential-following-reports-of-possible-deal-1362326/ Wed, 18 Nov 2026 20:54:40 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1362326

Culture Minister Marc Miller said Wednesday he won’t talk about any discussions the government has had with Meta about restoring news content to the company's platforms in Canada.

The post Minister says discussions with Meta ‘confidential’ following reports of possible deal appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Culture Minister Marc Miller said Wednesday he won’t talk about any discussions the government has had with Meta about restoring news content to the company’s platforms in Canada.

A day after Politico reported the company and the government were close to a deal before trade talks with the United States collapsed in August, Miller told reporters the discussions with Meta are confidential.

“Meta could always put news back online. They are the ones who removed it,” he said in French.

Meta blocked news from its platforms, including Facebook and Instagram, after the Online News Act became law in 2023. The bill requires Meta and Google to compensate news publishers for the use of their content. 

Citing an unnamed official, Politico said Meta put forward a proposal that would see it stop blocking news content in Canada, pursue commercial deals with publishers and fund two positions at the Canadian Journalism Collective.

In exchange, it would obtain an exemption from the law. Google already has an exemption, which it received after agreeing to pay $100 million to Canadian news outlets.

Politico reported the proposal was part of the wider U.S.-Canada trade negotiations. Ottawa shut down those talks in August after accusing the White House of demanding last-minute changes that threatened Canada’s sovereignty.

Meta declined to comment on the Politico report Wednesday.

Paul Deegan, president and CEO of the publishers’ group News Media Canada, said in an email Meta should only be exempt from the Online News Act if the company provides “fair compensation to Canadian news businesses just as Google has. They should not get our content for free.”

“Canada should not return to the dark days prior to the Online News Act when Google and Meta were picking the winners and losers” in Canadian media, he added.

In a brief interview, Deegan said before the Online News Act became law,Google and Meta were signing content licensing agreements with large news publishers but with not smaller independent publishers.

“You don’t want to have a situation where they’re only doing deals with the few, and then frankly potentially have outside influence with some of those publishers. Whereas if they’re doing deals with everyone, then everyone is under the same terms. And that’s really our concern if there’s any weakening of the Online News Act,” he said.

Kevin Desjardins, president and CEO of the Canadian Association of Broadcasters, said in an email a “deal is never a deal until it’s done, and how ‘close’ it was is in the eye of the beholder.”

He said the door has always been open to “Meta receiving an exemption from the Online News Act, as Google already has, provided that they offer something of true value to compensate news publishers for the various ways they make use of their content, including in their AI products.”

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 18, 2026.

Health Canada has authorized a new GLP-1 medication for weight loss that is a pill taken every day, rather than weekly injections.  

Eli Lilly’s Foundayo is approved for adults with obesity as well as those who are overweight and have at least one related medical problem, such as high blood pressure or sleep apnea.

In addition to promoting and maintaining weight loss, the pill is also approved to help treat Type 2 diabetes. 

Eli Lilly also makes the injectable drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound, which contain the active ingredient tirzepatide. Tirzepatide acts on two receptors associated with insulin production and hunger: GLP-1 and GIP. 

Competitor Novo Nordisk manufactures injectables Ozempic and Wegovy, which contain the active ingredient semaglutide. Semaglutide acts on GLP-1 receptors. Several other companies make generic semaglutide sold in Canada. 

The class of drugs known as GLP-1s have revolutionized weight-loss treatment and expertssay some patients may prefer to take a pill rather than an injection. 

There is another GLP-1 pill — Novo Nordisk’s Rybelsus — already on the market in Canada, but it is only approved for Type 2 diabetes management and not for weight loss.  

The active ingredient in Foundayo is orforglipron, a non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist.

Because it’s a smaller molecule than peptides semaglutide and tirzepatide, orforglipron can be taken orally and absorbed without being broken down by the digestive system, said Dr. Ehud Ur, an endocrinologist in Vancouver who is not associated with either Eli Lilly or Novo Nordisk. 

“It seems to be just as good as if not better” for weight loss as semaglutide and tirzepatide, he said.

The most common side effects of GLP-1 medications — both injectable and oral — include gastrointestinal issues, such as nausea or vomiting. 

Ur said whether he would prescribe Foundayo depends on the patient, partly because he is still waiting for clinical trial results on whether or not orforglipron has a cardiovascular benefit like semaglutide and tirzepatide do. 

Foundayo received Health Canada authorization on Nov. 13. Eli Lilly spokesperson Ethan Pigott said the company expects the pills to be available in pharmacies in January. 

There may soon be a second GLP-1 weight-loss pill option in Canada: competitor Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy pill, which is still awaiting Health Canada approval. 

Both Foundayo and the Wegovy pill are approved and available in the U.S. 

Even though Wegovy is made of the large peptide molecule semaglutide, Novo Nordisk is able to manufacture it in pill form by adding an ingredient called salcaprozate sodium to protect it from being broken down by digestive enzymes. 

Once the pill is swallowed, salcaprozate sodium, or SNAC, temporarily makes the area around it less acidic and helps it pass through the stomach lining into the bloodstream, Novo Nordisk spokesperson Kate Hanna said in an email on Wednesday.

Two former British Columbia NDP cabinet ministers disagree over the future direction of the party following its crushing defeat in last month’s provincial snap election.

Rick Glumac wants the party’s new leader to reconnect to the base, while Brenda Bailey warns against a turn toward the left.

Glumac, who was minister of state for artificial intelligence, said New Democrats need some “fresh voices” who have political experience, but can also connect with a “younger generation” of voters.

The former legislator, who lost his seat in the Oct. 24 election, said whoever can reconnect the NDP with its base and core values, like environmentalism and workers’ rights in an “uncompromising way,” should be the next leader.

He said that person “cannot be everything to everyone.”

They just don’t know it yet, but most British Columbians share the values of New Democrats, Glumac added, echoing comments from the late NDP premier John Horgan.

“But we need to be able to stand up for them, express them clearly and reconnect to British Columbians,” he said.

Bailey, who did not run in the election because she was undergoing cancer treatment, said she doesn’t know who could lead the party because it first needs to figure out its “essence.”

“When you have such a big loss, the natural thing to do is to return to the base, and that is where Opposition lives for a long time, frankly,” she said, noting that if the party does that it could languish in Opposition.

The former finance minister said the party is “probably going to move quite left” after last month’s election, which reduced it to 27 seats in the legislature after almost a decade in government.

But that would be a mistake, she said, in warning her party against emulating the federal NDP under their new leader Avi Lewis, who has proposed the introduction of a wealth tax among other measures.

“I would be very concerned with the (provincial) NDP to move that far left,” she said. “It’s very appealing. It all sounds very nice, but it is not achievable.”

Lewis ran unsuccessfully during the last federal election, finishing third in the riding of Vancouver Centre.

Glumac and Bailey offered the comments in separate interviews following the election, with an outcome that Bailey said was a “harsh judgment” on the leadership of outgoing premier David Eby.

But Eby, Bailey added, was not an ideologue.

“Eby was a practical person and did his best to govern a very broad group of people, all of whom had a veto, while trying to come up with practical solutions that benefited people in the province … to varying degrees of success.”

Glumac said Eby’s legacy will be recalled as short.

“People will probably remember the snap election and some other challenges that the party had at that time,” he said. “I can’t really say much more than that.”

New Democrats have appointed outgoing labour minister Jennifer Whiteside as their interim leader.

Departing NDP cabinet ministers Niki Sharma, Ravi Parmar and Ravi Kahlon have not ruled out running for the party’s leadership.

Glumac said in a social media post last month that the current moment requires “more than new messaging or a reshuffling of the same people at the top.”

He said the next leader must be able to motivate those who voted NDP in the past, but didn’t vote for the party last month.

“We have to energize them, get them excited about the future, and reconnect to our values,” he said.

Glumac said he is not really thinking about running himself, but added that he still very much believes in the NDP and its values.

“So, I’m going to be watching and I’m not going to be afraid to share my perspective and opinion along the way,” he said.

Bailey said she has “absolutely” no plans to run for the leadership, and “time will tell” whether she remains a New Democrat.

“I still don’t know who this party is, and that is the biggest question with people who are pro-business, (and) who care deeply about social issues, people like myself,” she says.

More than 285,000 people have signed a petition calling on the federal government to remove U.S. Ambassador Pete Hoekstra from Canada.

The petition accuses Hoekstra of making public statements that have undermined Canadian and U.S. relations and says he described the 2025 Canadian federal election campaign as “anti-American.”

Months after that federal election, Hoekstra said he was frustrated by the “elbows up” rhetoric used during the campaign.

The petition says Hoekstra accused Canada of interfering in U.S. domestic politics while making repeated statements on Canadian politics “inconsistent with diplomatic protocol.”

Hoekstra said during an interview on “The Really Big Show” podcast in October that political ads run by the province of Ontario last year could be interpreted as political interference.

The petition is now closed to new signatures. Most of those who signed live in Ontario or British Columbia.

Now that the petition has received more than the mandatory 500 signatures it needed to proceed, former Green Party leader Elizabeth May can present it to the House of Commons.

Speaking to The Canadian Press, May said she regularly brings forward petitions from her constituents.

Once the petition is presented to the House, the government has 45 calendar days to respond.

A spokesperson for the U.S. Embassy in Ottawa told The Canadian Press that the embassy is aware of the petition and declined to comment further.
